entities.title: Is a graduated document still under the convention?
entities.summary: Graduation replaces a document's status line with a ✅ line, and two other passages disagree on what that leaves: one says the document has left the convention, the other that the graduation check fails it.
entities.expected: The documents agree on whether a graduated document is under the convention, and the optional graduation check passes a correctly graduated document.
entities.observed: 02 § Graduation replaces the status line with "> ✅ This component is fully implemented, tested and free of known defects." The README says a document without the status line has not adopted the convention. 06's graduation check fails "a document under the convention" that "contains ✅ but no ⚠️ and no ❌", which a graduated document does if it is still under the convention.
entities.details: Either reading is consistent on its own: if a graduated document has left the convention, the graduation check never sees it; if it has not, the check as written fails every graduated document, because the line graduation keeps is a ✅. The repository is superseded and stays as it was written, so whether to fix the wording is the owner's call.

origin.description: Found while reading the documents to install human-assisted software development.

entities.title: Adoption says the agent-instructions lines do four things; they do six
entities.summary: 05 § 1 lists four things the lines in templates/agent-instructions.md do, and the block has two lines more.
entities.expected: 05 § 1's account of the block matches templates/agent-instructions.md.
entities.observed: 05 § 1 says the lines do four things: route agents to the documents, move the mark in the same commit, reserve ✅, and ban TODO. The block also tells agents to record a defect whose fix has to wait as a ❌, and to write a change log for every prompt that changes the code; the template calls the change-log line optional.
